:::{#exm-reals-in-complex}
#### Which complex numbers are real

R stores complex numbers as a real part and an imaginary part.
The code below converts the real number $7$ to a complex number
and reads the parts of three complex numbers.

```{r}
#| label: reals-in-complex
#| code-fold: false
z <- c(as.complex(7), 2 - 5i, 3 + 0i)
data.frame(z = z, re = Re(z), im = Im(z), is_real = Im(z) == 0)
```

The real number $7$ becomes the complex number `{r} format(z[1])`,
with imaginary part `{r} Im(z[1])`.
Of the `{r} length(z)` numbers,
`{r} sum(Im(z) == 0)` have imaginary part $0$,
and by @thm-reals-in-complex these are the real ones.
The number $2 - 5\,i$ is not real, because its imaginary part is `{r} Im(z[2])`.

:::
